title: Bilirubin trend under phototherapy
scenario: A 3-day-old term newborn is receiving intensive phototherapy for hyperbilirubinemia. Total serum bilirubin is measured every 6 hours to monitor the response.

questions.subject: Maternal-Newborn
questions.stem: How should the nurse interpret the bilirubin trend since phototherapy began?

options.text: The bilirubin is steadily declining, indicating the phototherapy is effective
The bilirubin is rising and phototherapy should be stopped
The bilirubin is unchanged, indicating no response to treatment
The bilirubin is fluctuating unpredictably and requires exchange transfusion

questions.rationale: The total serum bilirubin has fallen from 18.4 to 13.2 mg/dL over 18 hours, a steady decline that shows the newborn is responding appropriately to phototherapy.

questions.subject: Maternal-Newborn
questions.stem: While the newborn remains under phototherapy, which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Cover the newborn's eyes with opaque shields
Monitor temperature for hyperthermia or cold stress
Encourage frequent breastfeeding to promote bilirubin excretion
Assess skin turgor and intake and output for dehydration
Apply lotion to the skin to prevent drying under the lights
Dress the newborn fully to maximize warmth

questions.rationale: Eye protection, thermoregulation, frequent feeding, and hydration monitoring are core phototherapy interventions. Lotions can cause burns under the lights, and clothing the newborn reduces skin exposure needed for treatment.
